provenance.name: The dust cloud around the Ring Nebula's central star

products.label: Sahai et al. (2025), the dust shell fitted to Webb's mid-infrared light of the star
products.process: Draw a distance from the star so that the share of dots inside a radius grows as r^3.8 between 10.5 and 1,310 au, the density r^0.8 of the paper's shell; draw a direction uniform over the sphere; repeat 800 times. Distances and directions come from a seeded generator.
limitations: No grain has a measured position. Only the shell's inner and outer radius and its density law are the paper's; each dot's place is drawn from a seeded generator.

The cloud is invisible in visible light: its optical depth at 0.55 µm is 1.3e-8. The 800 dots are a display choice that makes visible a cloud Webb sees as extra light beyond about 5 µm and as extended emission in its 7.7, 10 and 11.3 µm images.

The paper's model is one-dimensional, so the dots are spread evenly over the sphere. The paper says the cloud is likely disk-like and has no direct information about its shape, so the round ball is a simplification, not a measured shape.
